title: Randomised study to evaluate metformin as an enhancer treatment and also to find out if it is effective and safe in daylight therapy for skin lesions.
official: Randomised, double-blind, multicentre clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical metformin in adjuvant to daylight photodynamic therapy in actinic keratoses.
summary: Main objective: To determine the efficacy and safety of topical metformin as an adjuvant to daylight photodynamic therapy (dPDT) with methyl aminolevulinate (MAL) in the treatment of actinic keratoses and the cancerisation field.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Males or females over 18 years of age.
2. Subjects with at least 5 actinic keratoses on face and/or scalp Olsen grade I and/or II (Olsen, 1991).
3. If women of childbearing capacity participate, they must use an effective method of contraception throughout the study.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients with predominantly Olsen grade 3 actinic keratoses.
2. Immunosuppressed patients.
3. Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
4. Have been treated for your actinic keratosis with surgery, cryotherapy, laser, radiotherapy, electrosurgery, 5-fluorouracil, diclofenac, imiquimod or retinoids 4 weeks previously.
5. Treatment with oral retinoids or nicotinamide in the previous 12 weeks.
6. Patients on oral treatment with metformin.
7. Patients with severe renal, hepatic and cardiac disease in whom oral metformin is contraindicated.
8. Patients with porphyria.
9. Patients with systemic diseases that may interfere with the results of the study.
10. Patients who are not expected to be able to follow the indications of the study.
11. Patients with hypersensitivity to any of the study drugs.
